newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline pulled higher by NYMEX unleaded.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline pulled higher by NYMEX unleaded.

text.p: NWE gasoline was propelled higher in afternoon trading on Friday by healthy gains in NYMEX unleaded futures, traders said.
NYMEX gasoline was trading nearly one cent up at 65.45 cents a gallon in midday trade in New York, having spent the last two weeks in the low 60s.
On the barge market, a European trading house bought 18,000 tonnes of Eurograde material at $206 fob ARA from at least five separate parties, traders said.

Some traders speculated this material could be headed for either the Mediterranean, which is tight in supply due to a spate of spring turnarounds, or to the east where Saudi Aramco recently tendered for 1.5 million barrels of 95 octane leaded gasoline.
Others said it was possible the purchase had been made simply to protect swap positions and that the material could end up being sold on and staying in the region.
Traders said that offers on Eurograde barges had risen to $208/10 in late trade. No physical deals were heard concluded at this level, although March paper was done at $209.
On the cargo front, traders said the trans-Atlantic arbitrage was just about open for large shipments.
But some noted that material going to the United States would soon have to adhere to lower volatility specifications which come into effect every spring.
"The material people are buying up at the moment is 13 psi, whereas the States want 9-10 psi which could add another $1-$2-1/2 if they have to process the material," he said.
